risks.name: Insufficient Sleep
risks.description: Sleep duration below optimal levels can impact cognitive function and immune system.
risks.solution: Aim for 7–8 hours per night and establish a consistent sleep schedule.

risks.name: High Blood Pressure
risks.description: Your blood pressure readings are too high.
risks.solution: Reduce sodium intake and continue daily exercise routine.

risks.name: Obesity Risk
risks.description: High BMI and body fat percentage indicate a risk of obesity-related conditions.
risks.solution: Focus on balanced diet, calorie tracking and consistent physical activity.

risks.name: Underweight Risk
risks.description: Your weight is too low for your height, which may lead to nutrient deficiencies or fatigue.
risks.solution: Increase healthy calorie intake and monitor progress weekly.

risks.name: Low Protein Intake
risks.description: Protein intake is below optimal levels, potentially impairing muscle recovery and hormone function.
risks.solution: Aim for 1.5–2g protein per kg body weight, depending on activity.

risks.name: High Junk Food Consumption
risks.solution: Reduce ultra-processed food intake, especially late at night and during stress phases.

risks.name: Excess Sugar Intake
risks.description: Your daily sugar intake exceeds recommended limits.
risks.solution: Cut down on sugary drinks, sweets and hidden sugars in packaged foods.

risks.name: Too Little Physical Activity
risks.description: Cardio and step count levels are consistently low.
risks.solution: Aim for at least 7000 steps daily and 2–3 cardio sessions per week.

risks.name: No Strength Training
risks.description: Lack of resistance training can lead to muscle loss and metabolic slowdown.
risks.solution: Include full-body strength workouts at least 2 times a week.

risks.name: Low Food Quality Score
risks.description: Your diet score indicates a poor nutritional profile.
risks.solution: Increase intake of whole foods, vegetables, lean proteins, and reduce junk.

risks.name: Low Sleep Continuity
risks.description: Your sleep is often interrupted or restless.
risks.solution: Establish a relaxing bedtime routine, limit screen time before bed.

risks.name: Low Mood After Sleep
risks.description: You often wake up feeling unrefreshed.
risks.solution: Improve sleep hygiene and evaluate stress levels and screen exposure before bed.

risks.name: Too Few Calories
risks.description: Calorie intake is too low over multiple days, risking undernourishment.
risks.solution: Ensure sufficient intake to support your activity level and growth.

risks.name: High Body Fat Percentage
risks.description: Your KFA (Körperfettanteil) is above optimal range for your age and sex.
risks.solution: Focus on reducing sugar and increasing physical activity, especially strength training.

risks.name: Abnormal Resting Heart Rate
risks.description: Your resting heart rate is unusually high or low, which may indicate stress or cardiovascular issues.
risks.solution: Improve sleep, nutrition and reduce stress. See a doctor if persistently abnormal.

risks.name: Blood Pressure Instability
risks.description: Your systolic or diastolic pressure fluctuates too much.
risks.solution: Monitor sodium and hydration levels, track stress and activity patterns.

risks.name: Multiple Days Without Exercise
risks.description: Several consecutive days without any physical activity detected.
risks.solution: Build a daily movement habit – even short walks help maintain metabolic health.

risks.name: Step Count Dropping
risks.description: Your weekly step average is decreasing.
risks.solution: Set small goals to increase walking (e.g. Go for a 30 min walk).

risks.name: Inconsistent Protein Intake
risks.description: Large daily fluctuations in protein can impair muscle retention.
risks.solution: Keep daily protein fairly stable by planning meals in advance.
